thread:
Marta: Heads up — sketch for a new add-on I'm calling ScaleGuard. Quick sync on launch gates, contract constraints, and minimal SKU shape?
Anand: High level — what does ScaleGuard buy customers?
Marta: Per-route reserved throughput (tokens/sec window) + a small bucket of soft fallback credits for bursts. Target: realtime apps and marketplaces that need steady tail latency.
Lee: Hmm metric choice matters. tokens/sec vs concurrency vs RPS? we bill tokens today.
Marta: Primary billing unit = reserved token/sec window, billed monthly as a capacity seat. Any usage beyond reserved first consumes burst credits, then metered overage at a premium rate.
Sofia: Operational question: when a customer's reservation is exhausted, what's the route? automatic fallback to a lower-cost model, queueing, or fail?
Ben: Also: customers hate complex knobs. Can we make this a simple SKU with clear behavioral bullets?
Marta: Proposed SKU names: ScaleGuard-10k, ScaleGuard-50k, ScaleGuard-200k. Pricing sketch below:
```
SKU             | reserved tokens/sec | monthly base | burst bucket | overage rate
ScaleGuard-10k  | 10k                 | $3,500       | 100k tokens  | $0.012/token
ScaleGuard-50k  | 50k                 | $12,000      | 500k tokens  | $0.010/token
ScaleGuard-200k | 200k                | $40,000      | 2M tokens    | $0.008/token
```
Anand: Launch criteria we should require: 2 pilot customers willing to sign a Beta contract, infra capacity for dedicated pools, egress/regional cap checks, and SLO definitions for failover. Also billing integration hooks.
Sofia: Legal needs to weigh in on refund policy for unused reserved capacity and caps on contractual burst.
Ben: From docs/marketing POV we need a one-pager that shows failback behavior in plain English and an example bill. I'll draft.
Lee: Perf/infra: do we need per-tenant KV cache isolation for latency guarantees? that has cost and deployment implications.
Marta: Noted — that's a tradeoff. For beta we can require cache pinning only for ScaleGuard-200k.
Anand: I'll own infra plan. Ops consideration: cap burst consumption per-customer to avoid noisy neighbors. Also need a metric and visualization in Console for reserved vs actual consumption.
Ben: Quick question: credits TTL? rolling 30 days or calendar month?
Anand: Default = rolling 30-day expiration for burst credits. Can be extended in contract.
deploy-bot: Reminder: RFC doc created — https://redwood/internal/scaleguard-rfc :lock:
Marta: Thanks — can @Ben draft the SKU page and @Anand produce the infra/capacity plan? target Beta in 6 weeks (milestone: pilot onboarding + console panels).
Ben: :thumbsup: I'll draft the SKU page and sample bill template.
Sofia: I'll sync with legal on contract language for caps/refunds Thu 11am — invite sent.
Lee: I'll run a perf estimate and call out when isolation is required.
Marta: Also want a quick fairness/privacy check to ensure one tenant's burst doesn't degrade others — @Sofia can add the acceptance test.
Sofia: Will add tests: noisy-neighbor scenarios + outage fallback audit.
Ben: lgtm
Marta: :rocket:
